questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion for emphasis in a conditional clause?
options: Only if you had studied harder would you have passed.
Had you studied harder, you would have passed.
You would have passed if you studied harder.
If you studied harder, you would have passed only then.
questions.answer: Had you studied harder, you would have passed.

questions.question: Which cleft sentence correctly restates the subject and object in a complex sentence?
options: The fact that it was raining was what delayed the project.
It was the project that was delayed because it was raining.
It was raining that made the project delay.
What delayed the project was it raining.
questions.answer: The fact that it was raining was what delayed the project.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive to express a hypothetical scenario?
options: She wishes she goes to Paris next year.
She wishes she would go to Paris next year.
She wishes she went to Paris next year.
She wishes she going to Paris next year.
questions.answer: She wishes she went to Paris next year.

questions.question: Which sentence uses ellipsis appropriately to avoid redundancy?
options: He said he would come, and he did. He came to the party.
He said he would come, so he came to the party.
He said he would come, and he came to the party, but he forgot his hat.
He said he would come, and he came to the party, but we didn’t invite him.
questions.answer: He said he would come, and he came to the party.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates the correct formal register with passive voice and conditional phrasing?
options: It was reported that the investigation was completed, but no conclusions were drawn.
The investigation was completed, and we drew no conclusions.
The conclusions were not drawn despite the investigation being completed.
They completed the investigation, but we didn’t draw any conclusions.
questions.answer: It was reported that the investigation was completed, but no conclusions were drawn.
